$schema_note: The map's drawn decisions, in the words they were asked for. Every row is either enforced by a rule this suite runs (test/app/lib/map-decisions.mjs) or pending with the question that blocks it. A decision that is not in this file is a decision nothing stops from reverting — which is the whole reason the file exists. Checked twice: test/app/map-decisions.test.mjs against the style module, and functional.mjs against the style a real browser is drawing.

rules.area-layers-are-shapes: Every World layer whose truth geometry is an area is painted as a fill. `covers` must account for every polygon layer in WORLD_LAYERS that is not named in a pending row — so a new area layer added later is covered on the day it lands, not the day someone remembers.
rules.min-line-width: A line layer is at least this many pixels wide at this zoom.
rules.line-weight-order: Line layers ranked heaviest first, asserted on the widths the style actually ships.
rules.paint-order: [under, over] — the second layer is painted after the first.
rules.has-casing: The layer ships a `-case` layer beneath it, wider than its own stroke.

decisions.asked: things like parking lots and thick wall areas use shapes over just lines
decisions.why: A parking lot outlined is a lot you read as a fence. Ground the guest walks on, parks on or stands in front of is an area in truth, so it is an area on the map — the outline is the shape's edge, never the whole of it.

decisions.asked: roller coasters displayed more visual and thicker on the map
decisions.why: Coaster track is the thing the park is famous for and the landmark a guest navigates by. Drawn at 1.6px it sat lighter than the midway it flies over and read as a stray scribble. The order is the whole World tier's line weight, so making the track heavier by making the midway thinner does not satisfy it. `boundary` is deliberately out of this chain — it is a hairline pending the wall decision below.

decisions.asked: roller coasters displayed more visual and thicker on the map
decisions.why: Heaviest-of-the-lines is a ranking and a ranking survives everything shrinking together. This is the floor: at the zoom a whole park fits on the screen the track is still three pixels of structure.
Track passes over the station house, the midway and the lot in life. Painted under any of them the ride is chopped into pieces wherever the park is busiest.

decisions.asked: paths read as walkways, not as gaps in the grass
decisions.why: One wide line in the ground colour under the path. Without it a midway crossing a lawn has no edge and reads as a gap in the grass.

decisions.asked: thick wall areas use shapes over just lines
decisions.question: `boundary` is the only area layer still painted as a bare 1.5px outline, and it is the only wall-like thing the map has: OpenStreetMap walls and fences (`barrier=wall`, `barrier=fence`) match no rule in packages/venue-builder/lib/osm-tags.mjs, so they are dropped before the app ever sees them. Filling `boundary` is not the fix — it sits above every ground layer in WORLD_LAYERS, so a fill there paints over the lake. Which does this decision mean: (a) the park perimeter drawn as a wall band with real thickness, (b) a new `wall` layer carried from OSM barriers through the builder, or (c) both?
decisions.why: Recorded rather than guessed. A decision nobody wrote down is the one that reverted; a decision guessed at wrong is the one that ships wrong and stays.
